\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Finite range as a natural-number range]
\lean{List.map_coe_finRange_eq_range}
\label{List.map_coe_finRange_eq_range}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, mapping each element of the finite range
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ to its underlying natural number gives the list $[0,\ldots,n-1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Merging nondecreasing lists]
\lean{List.Pairwise.merge}
\label{List.Pairwise.merge}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, and let $l_1,l_2$ be lists in $\alpha$, each
nondecreasing. Their merge is nondecreasing.
\end{theorem}

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in a predicate-defined set]
\lean{Set.mem_ofPred_eq}
\label{Set.mem_ofPred_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For any type $\alpha$, element $x\in\alpha$, and predicate $p:\alpha\to\mathrm{Prop}$,
membership of $x$ in the set $\{y\mid p(y)\}$ is equivalent to $p(x)$.
\end{theorem}
